glosses: A line or mark made by folding or doubling any pliable substance; hence, a similar mark, however produced.

examples.text: His pants had a nice sharp crease.
His shirt was brand new with visible creases from its store fold.

glosses: One of the white lines drawn on the pitch to show different areas of play; especially the popping crease, but also the bowling crease and the return crease.

examples.text: DRS showed he was out of the crease in a controversial run out review.

glosses: The circle around the goal, which no offensive players may enter during play, unless after scoring.
The area in front of each goal.
A crack.

examples.text: (To Ali G): My skin is so dry. So for being a bad boy, I want you to rub oil into me, paying special attention to my breasts and my batty crease.

glosses: To make a crease in; to wrinkle.
To undergo creasing; to form wrinkles.

examples.text: The bullet just creased his shoulder.

glosses: To laugh.

examples.text: I can't breathe, I'm creasing so hard.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas in Falten legen

glosses: To fold, crease, crumple, or wad.

examples.text: He crinkled the wrapper and threw it out.
The old man's lined face crinkled into a smile.

glosses: To rustle, as stiff cloth when moved.

examples.text: The green wheat crinkles like a lake.
All the rooms were full of crinkling silks.

glosses: A wrinkle, fold, crease, or unevenness.

examples.text: He observed the crinkles forming around his eyes and suddenly felt old.

glosses: The act of crinkling.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas in Falten legen

glosses: A crease, wrinkle, or irregular fold.
To rumple; to press into wrinkles by crushing together.

examples.text: He crumpled the note and threw it away.

glosses: To cause to collapse.

examples.text: He crumpled the car's body panels when he backed into a post.

glosses: To become wrinkled.

examples.text: The car's body panels crumpled when they hit the post.

glosses: To collapse; to surrender.

examples.text: The team's defensive strategy crumpled.
The defenders crumpled owing to exhaustion and dehydration.

Yes, Juve were unfortunate, in the extreme, with the deflected goal from Casemiro that gave Madrid a 2-1 lead just after the hour. From that point onwards, however, it was staggering to see a team renowned for defensive structure crumple this way.

translations.source_sense_description: etwas in Falten legen

glosses: Frotter fortement, meurtrir par une pression violente.

examples.text: Il s’est froissé un nerf.

glosses: Comprimer fortement une artère, pour arrêter une hémorragie.
Exercer une brusque pression contre le fleuret de l’adversaire.
Chiffonner.

examples.text: Je froissai le PV en boule avant de le jeter dans le caniveau.
Voici les signes avant-coureurs de la mort : dans les accès de folie, la phase du rire, fatale ; dans la démence, le geste répétitif d'effranger et de froisser les draps du lit, […].

glosses: Fâcher, blesser, heurter, choquer, surtout en parlant d’intérêts, d’opinions, de sentiments, etc.

examples.text: Et j’avouerai à Votre Majesté que je suis souvent froissé par la franchise de ses conseils.
Les spectateurs de cette scène, où tout froissait les sentiments vulgaires de la vie sociale, n'osaient se regarder.
Je comprends que ce mythe de la grève générale froisse beaucoup de gens sages à cause de son caractère d'infinité ; […].

Son « tu » me froissa un peu. Mais je lui répondis gaminement : « Tu trouves que j'ai engraissé ! » Il partit d'un fou rire. Et, à partir de ce jour, nous nous tutoyâmes et nous devînmes les meilleurs amis du monde.
— Et c’est pourquoi je voudrais te dire ceci… ne t’en froisse pas surtout… je serais désolé de te froisser… mais il faut que je te le dise…

glosses: Se piquer, se fâcher.

examples.text: Il s’est froissé de peu de chose.
Il se froisse d’un rien.
